title: EIP-7645: Alias ORIGIN to SENDER
description: Eliminate ORIGIN tech debt to lay groundwork for account abstraction and close security holes
author: Cyrus Adkisson (@cyrusadkisson), Eirik Ulversøy (@EirikUlversoy)
laymanDescription: Two EVM instructions report who is calling a contract: one gives the immediate caller, the other gives whoever started the whole transaction. The second has been discouraged since 2016, because a contract that trusts it can be tricked into acting on someone else's behalf. This proposal makes both return the immediate caller.
benefits: Closes phishing-style attacks that turn on the gap between initiator and immediate caller
Removes an obstacle that every account abstraction proposal must otherwise work around
Retires a feature deprecated since 2016, simplifying the EVM execution model
tradeoffs: Not backwards compatible: contracts relying on the distinction change behavior
The transaction initiator's address becomes unavailable to contracts entirely
The EIP names no concrete example of harmful breakage, so real impact is unmeasured
